step1_figure.description: Figure 24.29 shows a high-gain two-stage CMOS operational amplifier employing a cascode differential amplifier first stage and a push-pull class-AB output buffer stage with indirect feedback compensation (Cc = 240 fF connected to the source of M2T for high PSRR).

open_loop_dc_gain.description: Low-frequency open-loop differential voltage gain (A_OLDC = A1 * A2)

equation.formula: A_OLDC = A1 * A2 = [gm_diff * (ro_casc_n || ro_casc_p)] * [10 * (gmn + gmp) * (rop || ron) / 10]
equation.explanation: The overall DC gain is the product of the first-stage cascode diff-amp gain A1 (~500 V/V) and the push-pull output stage gain A2 (~31.6 V/V), giving ~15,800 V/V (84 dB).
equation.assumptions: Quiescent bias current of diff-amp ~20 uA, output buffer bias current ~100 uA, unloaded or high load resistance.

sky130_expected.calculation: In SKY130 with VDD=1.8V: for the first stage cascode, Rout1 ~ gm*ro^2 ~ 0.2 mS * (100k)^2 ~ 2 MOhm, giving A1 ~ gm1 * Rout1 ~ 0.2 mS * 2 MOhm ~ 400 V/V. For the second stage, gm_op ~ 1.2 mS, ro_out ~ 25 kOhm, giving A2 ~ 30 V/V. Total gain A_OLDC = 400 * 30 = 12,000 V/V = 81.6 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Device channel lengths in Sky130 (L >= 0.15 um) provide moderate self-gain per stage; cascoding in the first stage boosts open-loop gain to around 80 dB.

second_stage_gain.description: Low-frequency voltage gain of the push-pull class-AB output stage (A2)

equation.explanation: Calculates the small-signal gain of the output push-pull inverter/buffer stage biased at ~100 uA quiescent current.

sky130_expected.calculation: With I_D = 100 uA: ron = 1/(0.1 * 100 uA) = 100 kOhm, rop = 100 kOhm => ron || rop = 50 kOhm. gm_n ~ sqrt(2 * 270u * (50/0.15) * 100u) ~ 1.34 mS, gm_p ~ sqrt(2 * 50u * (100/0.15) * 100u) ~ 0.82 mS. |A2| ~ (1.34m + 0.82m) * 50k ~ 108 V/V (loaded by 10k RL drops to ~21 V/V = 26.4 dB; unloaded typically 30-35 dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends on the output transistor widths and quiescent bias current; matched to ~31.6 V/V (30 dB) nominal textbook derivation.

equation.formula: fun = A_OLDC * f3dB = gm1 / (2 * pi * Cc)
equation.explanation: With indirect compensation capacitor Cc connected to the low-impedance source terminal of M2T, the effective unity-gain frequency is set by gm1 / (2*pi*Cc).
equation.assumptions: Cc = 240 fF, non-dominant poles lie significantly above fun.

sky130_expected.calculation: gm1 of diff pair with I_D = 10 uA: gm1 = sqrt(2 * 270 uA/V^2 * (25/0.15) * 10 uA) ~ 0.3 mS. fun = 0.3 mS / (2 * pi * 240 fF) ~ 198 MHz. Accounting for parasitic capacitances at node 1 and the source of M2T, fun is typically 80 MHz to 150 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Indirect compensation achieves approximately 100 MHz unity-gain bandwidth with a small 240 fF capacitor as shown in Fig. 24.30.

phase_margin.description: Phase margin at the unity-gain frequency

equation.explanation: Measures closed-loop stability margin at the unity-gain frequency.
equation.assumptions: No heavy capacitive load on open-loop test, or standard 10 pF closed-loop load.

sky130_expected.calculation: The textbook reports PM ~ 70 degrees with Cc = 240 fF. In SKY130 with parasitic pole tracking, PM is expected between 60 and 75 degrees.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Indirect feedback pushes the non-dominant pole to higher frequencies compared to standard Miller compensation, ensuring comfortable 60-70 degree stability.

step_response_fall_time.description: High-to-low 10% to 90% transition / fall time driving 10 pF and 10k/1k load

equation.formula: t_fall = t(v(out)=0.18) - t(v(out)=0.82) for a step from 900 mV down to 100 mV
equation.explanation: Transient settling time for the output to transition low when driven by an input pulse through the inverting closed-loop configuration (gain = -1).
equation.assumptions: RL = 10k, CL = 10 pF, inverting configuration with 10k resistors as in Fig. 24.31.

sky130_expected.calculation: For CL = 10 pF discharged by output NMOS MON conducting peak current > 100 uA: SR = I / CL ~ 100 uA / 10 pF = 10 V/us = 10 mV/ns. For a 800 mV step, transition time ~ 800 mV / 10 mV/ns ~ 10-25 ns, consistent with Fig. 24.31 (~15-20 ns settling).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Large output stage MON (W=500/2) can sink ample transient current to rapidly discharge 10 pF.

step_response_rise_time.description: Low-to-high 10% to 90% transition / rise time driving 10 pF and 10k/1k load

equation.formula: t_rise = t(v(out)=0.82) - t(v(out)=0.18) for a step from 100 mV up to 900 mV
equation.explanation: Transient rise time for the output to transition high driven by PMOS pull-up device MOP.
equation.assumptions: RL = 10k, CL = 10 pF, inverting configuration with 10k resistors as in Fig. 24.31.

sky130_expected.calculation: Output PMOS MOP (W=1000/2) sources peak current > 100 uA charging 10 pF: slew rate ~ 100 uA / 10 pF = 10 V/us, giving rise time ~ 15-25 ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Symmetric drive from class-AB push-pull output buffer yields comparable rise and fall times under capacitive load.

quiescent_power.description: Total quiescent DC power dissipation of the op-amp with bias circuit

equation.explanation: Sum of bias branch currents in SUB_1 (~50 uA), diff-amp first stage (~30 uA), cascode load / bias branches (~20 uA), and push-pull output stage (~100 uA).

sky130_expected.calculation: Total quiescent current I_total ~ 50 uA + 30 uA + 20 uA + 100 uA ~ 200 uA. At VDD = 1.8V, P_diss = 1.8V * 200 uA = 360 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Dominated by the 100 uA class-AB output buffer bias plus core diff-amp and reference biasing.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench for CMOS op-amp with output buffer (Fig. 24.29 & Fig. 24.31) performing DC operating point, AC open-loop gain and phase analysis, and large-signal transient pulse response.
